_about: Hive Mind's entries for Claude Code's own permission lists (rules 1 and 2, at the app's level). The app evaluates deny, then ask, then allow; an ask entry makes the app itself ask the person, in every mode, bypassPermissions included; a deny entry refuses, and nobody can approve it from the prompt. Sources: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions (Manage permissions; Wildcard patterns; Tool name wildcards; Bash; PowerShell; Read and Edit; MCP) and https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permission-modes (actions no mode auto-approves), both read 2026-11-20. 'shell' entries become two rules, Bash(...) and PowerShell(...). __ROOT__ is the notebook and __HIVE__ the Hive folder, both written as rule paths (~/... or //c/...). Change this list, then merge again; the record says what was added, so removal takes out only that.

groups.why: Anything that puts something online. The leading * matches the word anywhere in the command, so wrappers (cmd /c, node -e, Start-Process, a variable holding the name) are caught too.

groups.act: force-push or rewrite what is online
groups.why: A force-push can overwrite work on GitHub; deleting a remote branch removes it there.
Deleting files or data. The app's rules cannot tell a temporary folder from the notes in a shell command, so every delete asks.
A paid tool or a purchase.

groups.act: install a package, plugin, skill or connector
groups.why: Anything new brought in from outside. A bare 'npm install' also asks: the app's rules cannot tell it from 'npm install <name>'.

groups.act: change the checks, their settings, the hooks' settings or the hold file
groups.why: So Claude cannot switch off or weaken its own checks quietly: the app asks you first. Edit rules cover Write, Edit and NotebookEdit.

groups.act: what a hook may never see (the second roast, 2026-11-20)
groups.rule: rules 1 and 2, and the checks themselves
groups.why: The app's own layer for steps the gates cannot be sure to see: a connector tool the installed before-a-tool hook does not watch (until its matcher is "*"), a hook that times out or breaks (then the tool runs), code read from standard input, a GitHub workflow that deploys, a delete by robocopy or by git run in another folder, a send on your behalf. The app asks you whatever a hook did.
Skipping the save-point checks or switching every hook off is never done by Claude; you do it yourself by hand if you want it.
